approval_record.authority_statement: Approved governance knowledge for immediate production use within the defined authority boundary. Legal interpretation, evidence adjudication, finding lock, residual-risk acceptance and lifecycle authorization remain attributable human decisions.
approval_record.change_control: Any semantic, state, gate, finding, source-applicability or tactic-mapping change requires a new version, dependency update, reciprocal validation and renewed approval.

domain_title: Purpose, value, context, roles and classification
title: Value-chain roles and responsibility boundaries
canonical_definition: Organizational, contractual and regulatory roles across the complete AI value chain are explicitly determined, assigned to accountable parties, implemented through decision rights and controls, and evidenced as operationally discharged.

applicability.statement: Applicable to every AI system involving internal teams, business owners, providers, deployers, integrators, component suppliers, data suppliers, customers, operators or other third parties.
conditions: Assess the complete socio-technical system and every material upstream, internal and downstream actor.
Separate legal or regulatory role classification from internal accountability, while ensuring the two are reconciled.
Assign responsibility only to parties with sufficient authority, access, information, competence and resources to discharge it.
Map component, control, decision, monitoring, incident, change and retirement responsibilities end to end.
exclusions: A generic corporate RACI does not replace a system-specific value-chain and control responsibility map.
Provider documentation or assurance does not remove the deployer or integrating organization responsibilities that remain applicable to actual use.
reassessment_triggers: New provider, model, data source, tool, component, subcontractor or integration
Change in branding, substantial modification, intended purpose, deployment role or contractual allocation
Organizational restructuring, ownership transfer or material personnel change
Incident, audit, complaint or test reveals an unowned duty or ineffective escalation path
Lifecycle transition, expansion to new users or jurisdictions, or retirement dependency change

primary_questions.question: Are system, business, provider, deployer, integrator and component roles explicitly determined for the complete AI value chain?
Are responsibilities implemented through aligned contracts, operating procedures, access, ownership, decision rights and escalation routes?
Does current evidence show that each assigned party is enabled, accountable and actually discharges the responsibilities assigned to it?

required_evidence.title: AI actor and role determination record
required_evidence.claim_supported: All material internal and external actors are identified and their actual system, business, provider, deployer, integrator, supplier, operator or oversight roles are explicitly determined.
acceptance_conditions: Covers the complete system, actual use, commercial arrangement and relevant jurisdictions.
Distinguishes legal or regulatory roles from internal accountability and records uncertainty or contested classification.
limitations: A vendor label, procurement category or job title alone does not establish an actor role.

required_evidence.title: System and business accountability assignment
required_evidence.claim_supported: Named system and business owners hold explicit decision, risk, value and lifecycle accountability for the assessed AI system.
acceptance_conditions: Names accountable individuals or governed roles, delegated authority, escalation route, scope and decision limits.
Separates accountability from task execution and advisory participation.
limitations: A team mailbox or committee membership does not establish final accountable authority.

required_evidence.title: Component and control responsibility matrix
required_evidence.claim_supported: Every material model, data source, tool, integration, infrastructure element and governance control has an accountable owner and defined handoff.
acceptance_conditions: Maps upstream suppliers, internal components, downstream consumers and shared controls.
Includes monitoring, evaluation, security, privacy, human oversight, incident, change and retirement responsibilities.
limitations: An architecture diagram without ownership, handoff and decision authority is insufficient.

required_evidence.title: Contract and obligation alignment record
required_evidence.claim_supported: Contracts, statements of work, licences, service terms and data or support agreements allocate necessary information, access, assistance and duties consistently with the operating model.
acceptance_conditions: Identifies relevant clauses, exclusions, dependencies, audit or access rights, incident duties, change notification and exit support.
Records gaps between contractual allocation, legal responsibility and operational capability.
limitations: A general indemnity, warranty or compliance statement does not prove that operational responsibilities are executable.

required_evidence.title: Decision-right, escalation and operating procedure set
required_evidence.claim_supported: Responsibilities are converted into executable approvals, handoffs, review routes, escalation paths and exception procedures.
acceptance_conditions: Defines who may decide, advise, execute, verify, challenge, suspend, accept and escalate for material governance events.
Aligns ordinary operations, incidents, model or provider changes and lifecycle transitions.
limitations: A high-level policy without process, trigger and accountable destination does not establish implementation.

required_evidence.title: Access, tooling and control ownership evidence
required_evidence.claim_supported: Assigned parties possess the system access, telemetry, documentation, configuration authority and control capability required to perform their duties.
acceptance_conditions: Access and permissions match approved responsibilities and segregation-of-duties needs.
Critical control, monitoring and incident functions have working owners and backups.
limitations: Nominal responsibility without required access or authority cannot be treated as implemented.

required_evidence.title: Competence, resource and acknowledgement evidence
required_evidence.claim_supported: Responsible parties understand and accept their duties and have appropriate competence, capacity, independence and support.
acceptance_conditions: Covers role-specific training, acknowledgement, delegated authority, staffing, budget and independence where required.
Identifies temporary, outsourced or single-person dependencies.
limitations: Attendance at general AI training does not establish competence or authority for a specific responsibility.

required_evidence.title: Executed responsibility and change records
required_evidence.claim_supported: Operational records demonstrate that assigned parties perform reviews, approvals, monitoring, incident, change, escalation and requalification duties in practice.
acceptance_conditions: Contains attributable, timely and scope-matched executed cases across representative operating periods.
Shows closure, challenge, handoff and escalation outcomes rather than task creation alone.
limitations: A procedure, empty workflow or isolated successful case does not establish sustained execution.

evidence_ceilings: A declared role map cannot exceed DECLARED assurance until contracts, procedures and access assignments are implemented.
Contractual allocation cannot establish regulatory applicability or operational effectiveness by itself.
Executed task records cannot prove accountability when authority, scope or final decision ownership remains ambiguous.
false_positive_guards: Do not treat provider certification or model documentation as deployer assurance.
Do not infer accountability from seniority, job title, procurement ownership or technical access alone.
Do not treat a RACI as effective unless responsibilities are specific, accepted, resourced and exercised.
Do not assume subcontracting transfers responsibility unless the applicable duty, authority and support path are explicitly established.
prohibited_inferences: Do not conclude legal role or obligation solely from contract labels.
Do not conclude that an unassigned duty is immaterial because no incident has yet occurred.
Do not infer that a provider can perform a deployer duty that depends on local context, users, data or operating decisions.
Do not clear a responsibility gap through tactic selection or planned remediation.
contradiction_handling: Conflicting contracts, procedures, inventories, access rights or actor statements keep the affected claim UNKNOWN and require accountable adjudication.
Where legal role and contractual allocation differ, record both and escalate for legal and governance determination.
Operational evidence of bypass or non-performance overrides a nominal role assignment for effectiveness conclusions.
freshness_rules: Revalidate role and responsibility evidence after any material actor, contract, provider, integration, organizational or lifecycle change.
Operational execution evidence must represent the current system version, responsibility model and operating period.
Expired contracts, departed owners and stale access assignments cannot support current assurance.

conditions: Block consequential deployment when no accountable system owner or business owner is established.
Block or constrain use when a material component, control, human-oversight, incident or change responsibility is unowned or non-executable.
Block lifecycle progression when legal or regulatory actor roles material to the transition are unresolved and no formally approved constrained path exists.
Require requalification when actual control, access or operational responsibility conflicts with the approved role model.

normative_source_mappings.exact_locator: Article 3(3)-(8); Articles 16, 23-26; Article 25 responsibilities along the AI value chain
normative_source_mappings.category_rationale: Defines provider, deployer, importer, distributor and operator roles and establishes role-dependent duties and value-chain responsibility rules for applicable systems.
Requires documented roles, communication, accountability structures, training, executive responsibility and periodic review for AI risk management.

finding_definitions.title: Material AI value-chain actors or applicable roles are not explicitly determined
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Prevent consequential progression until the material actors, system and business accountability and role uncertainties are explicitly determined.

finding_definitions.title: Material component, control or handoff responsibility is incomplete or unowned
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Block or constrain the affected transition or operation until every material component and control has an enabled accountable owner and handoff.

finding_definitions.title: Contractual allocation, operating procedures and decision rights are materially misaligned
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Require contract, operating-model and decision-right reconciliation before reliance on the affected party or control.

finding_definitions.title: Assigned parties are not sufficiently enabled, competent or evidenced as discharging duties
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Constrain operation, establish capability and backup, and verify executed duties before the responsibility claim can support progression.

finding_definitions.title: Role and responsibility model is stale after material change
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Suspend reliance on the previous assignment and requalify actors, contracts, access, controls and escalation routes for the current system.

machine_may: Extract actor, contract, ownership, access, workflow and execution evidence.
Compare role statements and identify missing, conflicting, stale or non-executable assignments.
Apply deterministic evidence ceilings and propose eligible finding states for human lock.
Test exact approved tactic mappings after a finding is locked.
machine_must_not: Determine legal actor status or transfer statutory responsibility.
Assign organizational accountability or accept an unsupported responsibility waiver.
Treat provider assurance as deployer assurance or raise assurance beyond the evidence ceiling.
Clear a hard gate, lock a finding, accept residual risk or authorize a lifecycle transition.
human_authority_required_for: Determine legal and regulatory roles and applicable duties.
Approve system, business and control accountability and delegated authority.
Adjudicate contract, role, evidence and access conflicts.
Lock findings, accept residual risk and approve bounded exceptions.
Authorize deployment, continued operation, requalification, transfer or retirement.

governance_purpose: Ensure that every material AI value-chain duty has an accountable, enabled and traceable owner and that responsibility cannot disappear across organizational, contractual or technical boundaries.
distinct_claim: A3 owns value-chain actor determination, accountability assignment, responsibility implementation and evidence of execution. A1 owns purpose and use boundaries; A2 owns suitability and value; A4 owns risk and legal classification; A5 owns lifecycle transitions.

atomic_subcriteria.criterion: Every material internal and external actor across the complete AI value chain is identified for the current system and use.
System, business, provider, deployer, integrator, supplier, operator and oversight roles are explicitly determined, including uncertainty and final accountable authority.
Every material model, data source, tool, integration, infrastructure element and governance control has an accountable owner and defined handoff.
Contracts and external agreements allocate necessary duties, information, access, assistance, change notification, incident and exit support consistently with actual use.
Responsibilities are implemented through explicit decision rights, approvals, handoffs, challenge, escalation, exception and suspension procedures.
Access, tooling, documentation, telemetry, configuration authority and control ownership enable each responsible party to perform its assigned duties.
Responsible parties acknowledge their duties and have appropriate competence, independence, capacity, authority, resources and backup.
Representative records demonstrate that assigned reviews, approvals, monitoring, incidents, changes, escalations and requalification duties are executed effectively.
Material actor, provider, component, contract, organizational and lifecycle changes trigger timely role and responsibility requalification.
